Subject: Confidential: EU pilot requirements and hosting question

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're preparing a small pilot (PHI adjacency, not full EHR ingest) to validate model outputs for clinical summarization. Legal and procurement have flagged two hard constraints: 1) all inference must run in an EU region, and 2) keys and audit logs must be under our control (KMS/HSM + 7-year audit retention). I've attached the regulatory checklist for your stack.

Two questions to start: given our compliance asks and modest Q4 traffic expectations (~15k requests/day, burst to 25k), do you recommend Redwood Private (VPC/air-gapped control plane) or Dedicated reserved capacity? We need an order-of-magnitude GPU slate + estimated lead time and a sense of incremental cost.

Subject: RE: Confidential: EU pilot requirements and hosting question

A quick sizing and comparison — see attached spreadsheet (gpu_estimate_breakdown.xlsx) for line-by-line math. Summary below.

Executive summary (pilot scale ~15k req/day, peak 25k):
- Private (VPC + customer KMS, private control plane):
  - Recommended baseline: 4 x A10G-equivalent (or 2 x A100-40GB with multi-instance) for steady-state inference with quantized 8-bit LLM family. Supports ~140 tokens/sec aggregate (batching + prefix cache).
  - Burst buffer: add 2 x A10G during peak dayparts.
  - Latency: p95 around 120–220ms per response (depends on prompt length and KV cache warm-up).
  - Lead time: 6–10 weeks (network provisioning, KMS/HSM integration, SOC evidence exchange).
  - Pros: full audit log control, keys retained by customer, easiest to meet strict legal language.
  - Cons: higher up-front setup, heavier ops involvement; slightly higher unit cost at low volumes.

- Dedicated (Reserved Redwood capacity in EU region):
  - Recommended baseline: 2 x A100-40GB (higher single-request throughput) with autoscale to burst via reserved pool (additional shared burst slots).
  - Latency: p95 ~90–180ms (better single-request latency due to denser GPU and Redwood runtime optimizations).
  - Lead time: 2–4 weeks to allocate reserved pool and configure tenancy.
  - Pros: lower monthly unit cost at scale, faster time-to-market, Redwood-managed logging with export options.
  - Cons: more work to guarantee customer-controlled KMS/HSM; legal may want contract language around log custody and retention.

Cost delta (rough): Private pilot setup premium ~+25–40% first 3 months vs Dedicated, then converges as committed utilization increases. Exact figures in attached spreadsheet.

Operational notes:
- For regulated workloads we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching and strict tokenization quotas to reduce required GPU headcount; both are supported in either hosting mode.
- If Stella requires HSM-backed keys in your tenancy, Private is straightforward; for Dedicated we can negotiate a contract appendix to certify log export and KMS integration (adds procurement cycles).

I'll be available Thursday for a quick sizing walk-through if helpful.

— Karthik
Deal Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: gpu_estimate_breakdown.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: EU pilot requirements and hosting question

Thanks Karthik — solid breakdown. A few procurement/SLA comments for Stella to consider:
- Private: procurement will want a platform license + setup fee and possibly an implementation SOW. SLA can be customer-specific (we can offer 99.9% with dedicated on-call and runbook), but restoration/RTO commitments depend on network/HSM timelines.
- Dedicated: easier to put into a usage commitment contract (monthly committed vCPU/GPU hours) and simpler crediting for outages. SLA easier to standardize but less control over key custody unless we bake export+rotation processes into the deal.

Suggested commercial approach for pilot:
1) Execute a short Private pilot SOW (60–90 days) focused on controls: KMS proof-of-concept, log export, and runbook validation. Price as a small fixed project + reduced monthly reserved capacity.
2) If output quality and ops checkpoints pass, convert to Dedicated reserved capacity at month 3–4 with a migration appendix (we can pre-negotiate migration credits).

Procurement timeline notes: PO for pilot typically ~2–4 weeks after SOW sign-off. If Stella needs us to accept stricter data custody clauses, loop legal early (we have templated clauses but may need redlines).

— Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — pulling the recommendations together into a short mutual action plan so procurement has concrete milestones. Proposed MAP: 

- Week 0: SOW sign-off (Private pilot, 60 days) + attach regulatory checklist (you provided).
- Week 1–2: Network + KMS integration (customer-side HSM keys) + Redwood stand-up of Private control plane in EU region; security review exchange.
- Week 3: Pilot launch (baseline 4 A10G equiv), smoke tests for latency and audit export.
- Week 6: Interim review; decision gate: if avg daily requests >18k and p95 latency <180ms we greenlight migration to Dedicated reserved slate.
- Week 9–12: Reserved capacity allocation + migration + production cutover if greenlit.

Ask for Stella: please confirm desired retention window for logs (we can provision 7 years as requested but need to confirm storage SLA and export format). Also confirm a primary procurement contact and any legal redline owners.

If that looks good I'll draft a short SOW and a PO estimate for the pilot.

— Ava
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
